original_question: If D is a real analytically bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n , is the d-bar Neumann problem globally real analytic hypoelliptic up to the boundary? - D. S. Tartakoff, U22393@UICVM.bitnet
correct_elements: Your draft is almost a verbatim transcription of the paper’s question. It correctly identifies the ambient space C^n, the hypotheses that the domain is bounded and pseudoconvex with real-analytic boundary (the paper phrases this as "real analytically bounded pseudoconvex domain"), the operator/problem involved (the ∂̄-Neumann problem), and the precise regularity property being asked about: global real-analytic hypoellipticity up to the boundary.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, D should be explicitly stated as a bounded pseudoconvex domain D ⊂ C^n with real-analytic boundary.
The quantifier is implicit in the paper: the question asks whether this holds for every such domain D (and, as written, for arbitrary n).

The phrase "the ∂̄-Neumann problem" is standard but implicit; a self-contained version should indicate that this is the usual ∂̄-Neumann problem for the complex Laplacian with ∂̄-Neumann boundary conditions.

The phrase "globally real analytic hypoelliptic up to the boundary" is not unpacked in the paper; a stand-alone version should indicate that the intended meaning is real-analytic regularity of solutions on the closure, i.e. up to every boundary point, when the data are real analytic.

The paper does not specify a form degree, so a completely formal operator-level statement would need to say whether one is asking at all relevant (0,q)-levels or leaving the usual ∂̄-Neumann setting implicit.
refined_question: Let D ⊂ C^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary. Is the standard ∂̄-Neumann problem on D globally real-analytic hypoelliptic up to the boundary; that is, do real-analytic data give rise to solutions that are real analytic on D̄?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 6.1.4 exactly: the wording in the paper is essentially the same, and it appears in Section 6.1 under the heading "The ∂̄ Neumann problem." There is no sharper official reformulation nearby, so the faithful refinement is to keep the question narrow and simply make the compressed phrasing stand-alone by spelling out the domain condition and the intended meaning of "globally real analytic hypoelliptic up to the boundary." I do not fold in the neighboring CR-manifold question (Problem 6.1.5) or the Hölder-estimate question (Problem 6.2.1), because those are distinct problems.
